newsitem.title: USA: Canadians charged with smuggling CFCs.
newsitem.headline: Canadians charged with smuggling CFCs.

text.p: Two Canadians have been charged with smuggling 85 tons of ozone-depleting chloroflourocarbons (CFCs) into the United States, federal authorities said on Wednesday.

Larry LeBlanc and Anne LeBlanc, of Fredericton, New Brunswick, are accused of violating U.S. environmental and customs laws by selling CFCs to auto repair shops where it was used to refill air conditioning equipment.

CFCs, often called Freon, are blamed for damaging the Earth's protective ozone layer. The chemical's production and distribution is being phased out under a 1987 international accord signed by both the United States and Canada.

According the U.S. authorities, the LeBlancs, who own a Fredericton auto dealership called City Sales Ltd, lied by saying they had a permit to export Freon to the United States through Houlton, Maine, between September 1993 and July 1994.
"Congress banned CFCs because they destroy part of our planet's atmosphere that protects us from the harmful effects of the sun," said Lois Schiffer, an assistant attorney general.

A U.S. official said the 85 tons of illegal shipments worth $3.4 million on the legal export market made the LeBlancs the fourth largest exporter of CFCs from Canada in 1994. The gas was enough to refill 110,000 car air conditioning units.
The LeBlancs were arrested Monday while on vacation in Rockport, Maine. A federal grand jury handed up a 21-count indictment against the couple Tuesday, who are now free on $50,000 bail.
Their attorney refused to comment and efforts to reach the couple were unsuccessful.
Scott Champion, a former employee of City Sales Ltd., pleaded guilty early this month to one count of violating the U.S. Clean Air Act and is awaiting sentencing, according to authorities.

Environment Canada had prohibited the LaBlancs' company, City Sales Ltd., from exporting CFCs after June 1993 because of a lack of permits, but U.S. officials did not know Wednesday if Canadian authorities would also file charges.
If convicted, the LeBlancs each face up to 85 years in prison and $5.2 million in fines. City Sales Ltd. faces up to $10.5 million in fines, authorities said.
